records.immediateBodies: CellAdmissionState enum + type library; RelayCellAdmissionSelector class (apply, inspect, persistIntent); free functions ensureCellAdmission, cellAdmissionState(s), setCellAdmissionBeforeBoundary, synchronizeCellAdmissionBoundary, lockedSelector, requireSelectorMatchesAdmission, normalizeMembership, encodeMembership/decodeMembership, stateFromEnabled/enabledForState/parseCellAdmissionState.
records.stateOwned: relay_admission_selectors singleton row (selector_id='general'); relay_admission_selector_intents (durable pre-commit CAS record, one row per attemptId); writes through to relay_cells.enabled / relay_cell_admission for every governed cell.
records.authLifecycle: Two-phase intent-then-commit CAS protocol. persistIntent durably records the attempt before the mutating transaction. apply() requires exact full-inventory membership coverage, exact generation match (or idempotent replay if already advanced), a mandatory SHA-256 membership fingerprint at generation 0 (optional above), re-verification that live admission state has not drifted from the selector's recorded membership, a one-way-door refusal to move any cell out of existingOnly back into migration/general once generation>0 (admission_selector_legacy_reenable), and a final optimistic-concurrency UPDATE...WHERE generation=? whose affected-row count is the real CAS gate.
records.failureCancel: An error after persistIntent commits leaves a durable, safely-retryable intent row; inspect() reports intent.state='unchanged' until a retry succeeds; persistIntent itself is idempotent for identical input, admission_selector_attempt_mismatch for divergent input under the same attemptId.
records.concurrency: No in-process mutex; relies entirely on the database's conditional UPDATE for single-winner-under-race. Confirmed by direct test: two concurrent apply() calls at the same expectedGeneration produce exactly one fulfilled and one rejected result.
records.realAssertionEvidence: cell-admission-selector.test.ts, 14/14 its read (lines 135-579): sticky-vs-placement interaction with an active selector, dormant-placement exclusion, unfenced-dead-cell non-recovery under a selector, atomic-commit + idempotent-replay + inspect(committed), generation-zero membership-drift rejection via AfterTransactionDatabase fault injection, admission-age preservation across a CAS, failed-CAS-intent persistence without membership mutation, duplicate/incomplete membership rejection before mutation, ambiguous-commit recovery via FailAfterIntentDatabase fault injection, concurrent-CAS single-winner + legacy-reenable refusal, selector-boundary survival across compatible/incompatible reconciliation.
records.sourceDefectsVsCorrections: None found in this file specifically.

records.immediateBodies: RelayMigrationCellRegistrar class with single public method add(input); free helpers normalizeMigrationCells, validateMigrationCell, membershipAfterAddition, requireExactAddedCells, insertCell, encodeCells. Imports lockedSelector/requireSelectorMatchesAdmission/encodeMembership/decodeMembership/normalizeMembership directly from cell-admission-selector.ts -- the one direct source-level dependency among the six files.
records.stateOwned: Inserts new relay_cells (enabled=1 unconditionally), relay_cell_regions, relay_cell_admission (admission_state='migration-only' unconditionally), relay_cell_connection_limits rows; writes relay_admission_selector_intents (shared table) and relay_admission_selector_cell_additions (operation-specific table storing exact cells_json); advances the shared relay_admission_selectors row.
records.authLifecycle: Requires the selector boundary already active (generation>=1, else admission_selector_boundary_inactive) -- addition only follows cutover, never precedes it. Full per-cell (id/url length, capacity 1..100000, legal hard cap, unobserved bound within relayCellAdmissionBounds, legal region) and per-batch (1..128 cells, no duplicate id/url) validation, then requires none of the added cells already exist in inventory. Idempotent-replay branch cross-checks BOTH the shared intent row and the operation-specific additions row exist together (torn write between the two is a hard admission_selector_attempt_mismatch, not treated as an ambiguous-retry case), and on confirmed prior success re-verifies every added cell's live state field-by-field via requireExactAddedCells -- stricter than apply()'s own replay check.
records.failureCancel: Same intent-durability shape as apply(); an interrupted commit after intents/additions rows are written but before the selector advances is recoverable by retry. No dedicated fault-injection test for this file was found (unlike cell-admission-selector.test.ts's FailAfterIntentDatabase/AfterTransactionDatabase harnesses).
records.concurrency: Same conditional-UPDATE CAS mechanism as apply(), inheriting the same single-winner-under-race property by direct reading, but NO test in this codebase was found exercising two concurrent addMigrationCells calls the way apply()'s concurrency is explicitly tested -- named as a discriminating gap below.
records.realAssertionEvidence: cell-admission-selector.test.ts, last 2 of its 14 its (lines 467-579): 'atomically adds exact migration-only cells after the selector boundary' (confirms membership update, idempotent replay, cellDeploymentStatus reflecting the new cell's exact connection capacity) and 'rejects additive cells before cutover and exact-attempt config reuse' (confirms admission_selector_boundary_inactive pre-cutover, admission_selector_attempt_mismatch on a changed cell field under the same attemptId, and admission_selector_attempt_mismatch when a subsequent apply() call reuses the same attemptId with different membership).

records.immediateBodies: AssignmentIdentityQueue class, single public method run<T>(identity, operation): Promise<T>, implementing a per-key serial-execution queue via a Map<string, Promise<void>> of chained tail promises keyed by JSON.stringify([userId, relayHostId]).
records.stateOwned: Purely in-memory, per-process (the tails map); no database, no cross-process coordination -- process-local serialization only.
records.authLifecycle: None -- pure concurrency primitive, no authorization surface.
records.failureCancel: run() chains via previous.catch(()=>undefined).then(operation) -- a rejected prior operation does NOT block or fail the next queued operation for the same key; the queue's own tail-tracking similarly swallows both outcomes. The caller of run() still receives the ORIGINAL rejection via return await result -- only the internal chain is failure-transparent, confirmed by the 'continues after a rejected operation' test.
records.concurrency: Confirmed by direct test evidence: same-identity operations are strictly serialized (execution-order assertion via a deferred promise gate); different-identity operations run fully concurrently with no queueing (second identity completes and is observed before the first identity's still-blocked operation releases). The finally-block guard `if (this.tails.get(key) === tail) this.tails.delete(key)` prevents a completed operation from deleting a newer tail that has since replaced it -- confirmed correct by reading, but no test in the 70-line file specifically exercises a three-or-more-operation interleaving that would distinguish this guard firing correctly vs. incorrectly (named as a discriminating gap below).
records.realAssertionEvidence: assignment-identity-queue.test.ts, 3/3 its read (all 70 lines): same-identity serialization, cross-identity concurrency, rejection-does-not-block-queue.
